title: Anthropic Opens 34% Higher in Nasdaq Debut, Briefly Worth $2 Trillion
excerpt: The Claude maker's shares opened at $111.50 against an $83 IPO price, completing a record $81.3 billion raise before slipping back below $100 in the first hour.
body:
• Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, 34% above the $83 IPO price, briefly valuing the Claude maker at about $2 trillion.
  • The $81.3 billion offering — 980 million shares — is the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's $75 billion raise in June; the sale is expected to close on November 20.
  • The stock gave back part of the pop within the first hour, slipping below $100, and traded in the mid-$90s by early afternoon.
  • Shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT; at about $98 the company was worth roughly $1.8 trillion, still well above its $1.5 trillion valuation at the offer price.

Anthropic hit $2 trillion in market value in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, as investors rushed to own a stake in the first frontier AI company to trade publicly. The stock opened at $111.50, 34% higher than the IPO price of $83, according to Reuters, before slipping back below $100 within the first hour of trading and changing hands in the mid-$90s by early afternoon.

The debut completes a two-day sequence that began with pricing on Wednesday night. Anthropic said it priced 980 million Class A shares at $83.00 — above the $70 to $78 range in its filing — with 956,351,354 shares sold by the company and 23,648,646 by selling stockholders. The registration statement was declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 18, and the offering is expected to close on November 20. We covered the pricing, and what the $1.5 trillion valuation rests on, in our earlier report.

A record raise, and a private placement on top

At $81.3 billion, the offering surpasses the $75 billion SpaceX raised in its June IPO, Reuters reported, and proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to buy additional shares. The figure currently sits at over $107 billion including a separate $26 billion private placement, whose investors were AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet's Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. The underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, stand to earn a $550 million fee, according to a regulatory filing cited by Reuters.

Based on the IPO price, chief executive Dario Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10% of the company, held stakes valued at nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation from the filing. TechCrunch reported that the opening price put Anthropic's market capitalisation above Meta, Tesla and Walmart, with only Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia and Microsoft valued higher.

"Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing. If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top."

— Dario Amodei, Anthropic CEO, before the opening bell, via TechCrunch

An unusual debut dividend: charity

The listing also sets up one of the largest philanthropic windfalls from a single IPO. TechCrunch reported that Anthropic's Public Benefit Fund was allotted 5% of the company's shares — almost 850 million — worth an endowment of about $80 billion at a trading price of about $95, with further 2% increases triggered each time the valuation grows more than 50% above the IPO price. The fund's first commitment was $200 million to study the impact of AI on workers. Employees have separately pledged shares to causes of their choice, with the company matching 3-to-1 for longer-tenured staff and 1-to-1 for newer staff; TechCrunch estimated the pledges and matches could total about $156 billion if employees make good on them.

The sceptics' case

Demand held up through a broader tech selloff, but the valuation drew open scepticism. "Anthropic is a one-trick pony. People compare it with Amazon because even Amazon lost money for several years, but Anthropic won't have that luxury," Bill Gunderson, a partner at GCG Advisory Partners, told Reuters. "They've got to get to profitability soon." Reuters also noted that Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google — the scale of spending the new cash is meant to underwrite — and that Amodei told CNBC the company may tap debt markets in future.

What happens next

The offering closes on November 20. After that, attention turns to the stock's first earnings report as a public company and to whether the debut reopens the IPO window for other AI firms: Reuters reported that Anthropic's arch-rival OpenAI is eyeing a 2027 listing. For now, as Direxion's head of capital markets Jake Behan put it to Reuters before the debut, the week has been "a referendum on AI" — Nvidia's earnings on Tuesday supplied the read on the buildout, and Anthropic's first day supplied the read on investor appetite.
